proof_summary: Assuming finiteness bounds all bases \(x\) for which \(x^4+1\) is prime; positivity then gives, for every \(n>2\), a decomposition \(n=p+q\) with \(x=\phi(p)\phi(q)\) under that bound. Since \(\phi(p)=p-1\) and \(q\le 2\phi(q)^2\), both \(p\) and \(q\) are uniformly bounded, contradicting the existence of arbitrarily large \(n=p+q\).
